accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS 2.MD.10 (picture graph and bar graph with a single-unit scale, up to four categories, put-together, take-apart and compare problems) and NC 2013 Y2 Statistics (interpret and construct simple pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams and tables; ask and answer questions about totals and comparisons). Every number recomputed: votes 5, 3, 6, 2 total 16; apple or banana 5 + 3 = 8; not grape 16 − 6 = 10 = 5 + 3 + 2; grape v pear 6 − 2 = 4; challenge pets 7, 5, 2, 4: 7 − 2 = 5, 5 + 4 = 9, total 18, 7 − 3 = 4 (rabbit), 18 − 7 = 11. Parameterised items checked at range corners (p1 1..8, p5 7..17, m2 6..18, m5 2..7); all non-negative.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented graph-reading errors (Friel, Curcio and Bright 2001 on graph comprehension; NCETM Y2 statistics notes; Bright and Friel 1998 on counting gridlines): counting the 0 line as 1 so bars end one too high (setBar message at one above, prediction 2, challenge 'zero', m3), reading a picture as worth 2 after pictogram keys (prediction 1 option '3, one for every 2'), adding when asked how many more (prediction 3, challenge 'add', m4), reading one bar instead of the gap (challenge 'bar'), totalling categories instead of votes (challenge 'groups') and putting the category label on the counting axis (label feedback).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbgraph is a graph-building lab on a 0 to 8 single-unit scale: tap columns to add one picture per vote, drag bar tops onto the right line, place a title and both axis labels, tap the bars a question needs while the sum builds, and slide a level line from the grape top to the pear top so the gap is shaded. flagtally is about tallying in gates of five, pictograms with a key of 2 and block diagrams; flagbarm uses bar models for word problems, not data graphs. Max 6-shingle similarity 5.5% (flag_mbhab.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child builds the graph before reading it: pictures turn green only when the count matches the card, bars snap to lines so the reading-the-line rule is felt, the label slots show which axis counts, the running sum (5 + 3 = 8; 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 next to 16 − 6) shows put-together and take-apart give matching answers, and the yellow gap appears only when the level line sits on the pear bar, so 'how many more = gap' is seen.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options disproved on screen: '3, one for every 2' (one picture per child gives 6), 'one line higher, counting the 0 line as 1' (the bar for 6 stops on the 6 line and the lab names the zero slip), and '8, add both bars' for how many more (the shaded gap is 4).

challenge_feedback.evidence: slip() has eleven distinct messages (add, bar, gap, one, groups, tallest, fewer, far, copy, zero, mix), each naming the slip and the fix, e.g. '4 is the number of pets on the graph, not children. Add all the bars.' In-lab wrong moves are specific too: an extra picture says how many to take off, a wrong bar tap explains 'or' and 'did not choose', and each wrong label slot says which axis counts.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience: kid FK 1.2, adult FK 8.1. Kid text uses picture, bar, line, top, gap with one worked comparison (grape 6, pear 2, gap 4); canvas captions shrink to fit at 360 px rather than clip.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap 1.5% with Pictograms and tally charts, under 12% with every lesson). Kid paragraphs: picture graph; bar graph; title and axes; add, take apart, compare. Adult paragraphs: curriculum and key words; named mistakes; why a single-unit scale matters before scaled graphs; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at 360 px Android (light and dark) and iPhone 13 (light), plus a scrolled view of the label step: the scale numbers, fruit names, rotated side label and bottom label all fit with no overlap; bars are 56% of a column wide; the level line spans the whole frame so it can be grabbed anywhere; control buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has buttons ('Add an apple picture', 'Grape bar up one', 'Put the label Fruit on the bottom axis', 'Use the pear bar', 'Move the level line down one'). say() updates the canvas aria-label and narration after each action, including the current bar value and level line. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
